item.title: Apple Store employees accused of signing customers up for subscriptions without consent
item.description:
Consumer rights advocate Louis Rossmann has accused some Apple Store employees of enrolling customers in auto-renewing subscription trials — including Apple One — without their informed consent, in a series of YouTube videos posted over the past two weeks. The alleged pattern starts with an employee offering to scan a QR code for a personalized shopping experience called "Connect and Personalize." That flow, Rossmann claims, can end with customers unknowingly signed up for paid trials.

The accusations land at a sensitive moment for Apple, which leans heavily on services revenue and markets itself on user trust. Apple has not yet publicly responded in the coverage. If the claims hold up, expect scrutiny of the in-store signup flow and whether the company tightens how employees present trials — or faces regulatory attention over consent practices at retail.

Sources

  • MacRumors: Apple Store Subscription Sign-Up Controversy Exposed

item.title: Nvidia opens investigation into CEO Jensen Huang after relationship with alleged Chinese spy
item.description:
Nvidia announced Sunday that it is investigating its chief executive and co-founder, Jensen Huang, after he acknowledged to the board that he had been intimate with a business executive whom U.S. intelligence determined to be a Chinese spy. The woman, named Alice Huang, was under surveillance that reportedly showed her feeding information directly to Beijing.

The fallout goes beyond a personal scandal: Huang is one of the most powerful figures in the global chip industry, and Nvidia's chips sit at the center of U.S.-China technology tensions. Nvidia says it does not share classified information with customers and denies Huang pressed the government to change chip export policy. The investigation is now underway, and the episode is likely to draw further attention to how U.S. intelligence views the company's China relationships.

Sources

  • Daring Fireball: Jensen Huang Betrayed Nvidia, Not Just His Family
  • Daring Fireball: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Was Banging a Chinese Spy, Who Was Feeding Information Back to Beijing

item.title: Siri could become "more like an agent" as early as next year
item.description:
Apple's long-awaited personalized Siri finally shipped with iOS 27, but it still doesn't proactively take actions for users the way rival agents do. That may change soon: Bloomberg's Mark Gurman reports Apple could make Siri function "more like an agent" as early as next year, able to keep track of goals, figure out what needs to happen next, and keep pursuing objectives without being prompted step by step.

The timeline is still gradual. Siri AI in the iOS 27.3 developer beta can already handle more tasks in first-party apps, but deeper control of Apple apps — and any expansion to third-party apps — isn't expected until spring 2027. The direction is clear, though: Apple is moving Siri from a command-response assistant toward a proactive agent, even if it's arriving later than competitors.

Sources

  • MacRumors: Siri AI Rumored to Become 'More Like an Agent' as Early as Next Year
  • 9to5Mac: Apple aiming to make Siri ‘more like an agent’ as soon as next year: report
  • AppleInsider: Siri AI won't get more control of Apple apps until Spring 2027

item.title: New CEO John Ternus is pushing to speed up Apple's software — and the Siri chief may leave
item.description:
New Apple CEO John Ternus is reportedly pressing software chief Craig Federighi to accelerate Apple's software roadmap, according to Bloomberg's Mark Gurman — the latest sign that the company's pace in AI has become a top-level concern. The pressure comes as Apple faces persistent criticism that it is moving too slowly to keep up with rivals.

At the same time, Mike Rockwell — who led the Vision Pro and then took over Siri AI for its 2026 revamp — is reportedly considering stepping down from the Siri role during 2027, or leaving Apple altogether. Gurman also notes differing views among leadership about AI strategy. Taken together, the reports suggest Apple's AI leadership is in flux at the very moment the new CEO is demanding faster results.

Sources

  • 9to5Mac: Report: John Ternus pushing Craig Federighi to speed up Apple software engineering

item.title: Apple is changing how it builds iOS 28 and macOS 28 to give engineers more room to create
item.description:
Apple has reworked its development schedule for iOS 28, macOS 28, and the rest of next year's operating systems. The company typically splits each year's OS development into three stages of four weeks of coding followed by four weeks of "convergence," where features get integrated. For the 28 generation, the first stage stretched to six weeks of coding, giving engineers more creative time before the convergence crunch.

The tweak may sound bureaucratic, but the way work is scheduled shapes what gets built — more uninterrupted coding time early on could mean more ambitious features, or at least fewer half-finished ones. It's also a practical response to the same pressure behind the Ternus push: Apple wants its software teams moving faster without sacrificing quality.

Sources

  • MacRumors: Apple Taking New Approach to Developing iOS 28 and macOS 28
  • AppleInsider: Apple's iOS 28 schedule shift helps engineers get more creative

item.title: Apple saved $2.7B in taxes this year by routing finances through Singapore
item.description:
Apple saved $2.7 billion in taxes in 2026 by funneling its finances through Singapore, according to a Financial Times report based on an annual Apple disclosure filed under U.S. reporting rules. Ireland has long been Apple's best-known tax-efficient hub, but Singapore's incentives delivered an even better result this year.

For a company of Apple's scale, tax strategy is as much a part of the financial story as product sales — and the Singapore route shows how multinationals keep shifting structures as rules and incentives change. Expect the disclosure to draw the usual questions from regulators and tax watchdogs, even though the arrangement is legal under current rules.

Sources

  • AppleInsider: Apple saves $2.7B in taxes by funnelling finances through Singapore

item.title: macOS 27.3 may rein in AI agents asking for Full Disk Access
item.description:
Apple announced last month it would tighten privacy controls in a future macOS update after AI agents began requesting Full Disk Access and then using users' data in ways they hadn't fully understood. Now there's a first look at how the changes might work in macOS 27.3, with a more explicit, granular permission flow for agents requesting broad access to your files.

The move matters because AI agents are increasingly asking for the keys to the kingdom — full disk access — to do their jobs, and the old one-tap grant didn't make the stakes clear. A stricter, clearer flow should keep users from accidentally handing an agent access to everything on their Mac, while still letting power users who know what they're doing opt in.

Sources

  • 9to5Mac: macOS 27.3 could change how you grant AI agents Full Disk Access, here’s how

item.title: Apple launched five products this week, with two more on the way
item.description:
Apple is having a very busy November. Five new products launched on Friday, November 6, following pre-orders that opened the week before, and two more products are still on tap for next week. On the software side, Apple released the first betas of iOS 27.3 and related updates, bringing a number of tweaks and new features.

The pace is notable even by Apple's standards — a week into November and the company is still rolling out hardware. Looking further ahead, the pipeline for the first half of 2027 is already taking shape, with more product launches expected in the coming months. For anyone holding off on a purchase, the flood of new hardware also means the previous generation is about to get cheaper, which ties into the early Black Friday deals already surfacing.

Sources

  • MacRumors: Top Stories: Apple Product Launches, iOS 27.3 Beta, and More

item.title: Early Black Friday deals: MacBook Air $250 off, Apple Watch Ultra 3 clearance, AirPods discounts
item.description:
Black Friday is November 27 this year, but the Apple deals are already live. The highlights include the MacBook Air at $250 off, the Apple Watch Ultra 3 on clearance at $250 off, the new Apple Watch Ultra 4 at nearly $100 off, AirPods Pro 3 down $50, and AirPods Max 2 at $100 off in all colors. Amazon has also brought back the pre-order deal on the new Apple TV 4K ahead of its release next week, alongside pre-order deals on the new Apple HomeView.

Several of these are at or near all-time low prices, so if you've been waiting on a MacBook Air, a watch upgrade, or new AirPods, this is the window. The usual caveat applies: the best deals tend to sell through as Black Friday itself approaches, so waiting for the day itself may not pay off.

item.title: iPhone Air 2 arrives next spring with a second camera — and more to prove
item.description:
Apple will unveil the second-generation iPhone Air next spring, after taking extra time to rework the design and add a second camera. But the phone's position in the lineup has changed since the first Air launched: the iPhone Duo foldable is now the flashy, attention-grabbing device, and the Air can no longer coast on being the cool one.

That means the Air 2 has to appeal to a much wider audience than just enthusiasts drawn to its thinness. The added camera addresses one of the original's most obvious compromises, but the real question is whether Apple can give the Air a clear reason to exist alongside the Duo and the standard iPhone. Spring is still months away, so expect more details to leak before the announcement.

Sources

  • 9to5Mac: iPhone Air 2 is coming next year, here’s why it has more to prove than ever

item.title: Chromagraph Camera brings a film look to iPhone photos
item.description:
Movie director Rian Johnson surprised everyone last week by launching Chromagraph Camera, a new iPhone camera app that reimagines what a smartphone photo should look like. The pitch is simple: iPhone photos tend to look overprocessed, and while the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Duo's new film texture option helps, it goes a bit too far in the other direction.

Chromagraph lands in the sweet spot, according to early hands-on impressions — a film-like look that feels natural rather than exaggerated. For anyone who has been frustrated by the computational, over-sharpened feel of default iPhone photos, this is the most promising third-party camera app to arrive in a while, and it comes from a filmmaker who clearly cares about the image.

Sources

  • 9to5Mac: Chromagraph Camera is exactly the camera app I’ve been looking for on iPhone

item.title: New MacBook Pros get a glowing logo — and a free app to control it
item.description:
The new MacBook Pros brought back the glowing Apple logo on the lid, and designer Juan Buis has already shipped an app to control it. Backglow lets you adjust the logo's brightness independently of the display, turn it off entirely with one click instead of resorting to Terminal, or enable a "Breathe" mode that gently pulses the light like the sleep indicator on older MacBooks. The free version covers all of that; a one-time $9 payment unlocks the Pro features.

Meanwhile, the new machines themselves continue to draw attention — John Gruber joined Tyler Stalman and David Altizer's Full Stack Creator show this week to talk about the new MacBook Pros and their PROLED XDR displays, which he covered at length in his "Touch and Glow" piece. The glowing logo is a fun throwback, but the display is the real story of this generation.

Sources

  • MacRumors: 'Backglow' Lets You Customize New MacBook Pro's Glowing Apple Logo
  • Daring Fireball: Yours Truly on Full Stack Creator, Talking About the New MacBook Pros With PROLED XDR Displays

item.title: Apple's touchscreen OLED MacBook Pro arrives, glowing logo and all
item.description:
Apple's new MacBook Pro with a PROLED XDR touchscreen display is now in customers' hands, five years after the last redesign. The 14-inch model is about half a millimeter thinner and just over three pounds, with the 16-inch nearly a millimeter thinner, and both bring back the glowing Apple logo on the lid — a detail absent for a decade. The logo lights up whenever the Mac is awake and adjusts with screen brightness and ambient light.

Early verdicts are mixed on who the machine is actually for. Starting at $2,899 for the 14-inch and $3,399 for the 16-inch, it sits hundreds above the already excellent standard MacBook Pro, and reviewers question whether the touchscreen justifies the premium. If you don't love the glow, Apple explains how to disable it in a support document — but only via a Terminal command, with no toggle in Settings.

item.title: OLED iPad mini and M6 iMac hit stores as Apple tees up two more launches next week
item.description:
The eighth-generation iPad mini with an OLED display and the M6 iMac are available starting today, alongside the new MacBook Pros, with first pre-orders arriving at customers' doors. The iPad mini's 8.5-inch Super Retina XDR display reaches 1,200 nits of peak brightness with a 2,000,000:1 contrast ratio, and a nano-texture glass option is available on higher storage tiers.

Apple's launch wave isn't done yet: the all-new HomeView smart home hub and the fourth-generation Apple TV 4K are set for release next Friday, November 13. Since late August, Apple has announced more than 25 new devices and accessories, and no further major hardware releases are expected for the rest of the year.

item.title: Over 100,000 apps are now optimized for the iPhone Duo
item.description:
Two weeks after the iPhone Duo launched, Apple says well over 100,000 apps have been optimized for its twin screens, with thousands more added daily. The count covers apps built with the iOS 27.1 SDK or later, meaning they fill the full width of the inner and outer displays. Apple's developer relations chief called the response the strongest for a new device since the iPad in 2010.

The app gap was widely seen as the Duo's Achilles' heel at launch, but the pace of updates is closing it fast. Developers keep finding creative uses for the foldable form factor, from marble mazes that use the hinge as a ramp to productivity setups pairing the phone with an external keyboard — and MacStories' roundup suggests the Duo is increasingly working as a pocket computer, not just a phone.

item.title: iOS 27.3 beta brings a redesigned Health app and more Siri AI powers
item.description:
Apple released the first iOS 27.3 beta this week, and it's shaping up to be a substantial update. Headlining the changes is a redesigned Health app, alongside expanded Siri AI actions across Apple's apps — unsubscribing from mailing lists, organizing files, managing Safari tabs, and adding saved locations or toggling weather alerts in the Weather app. The watchOS 27.3 beta adds Siri Recap to the latest Apple Watch models, plus conversation summaries.

Separately, Apple has effectively ended the Siri AI waitlist: its support document now says the waitlist applies only during periods of high demand, and testers are getting instant access. Apple also held an online Apple Intelligence Group Lab this week walking developers through how Siri AI uses schemas, tools, and skills — a sign Apple is leaning on third-party developers to extend the assistant.

item.title: Next year's iPhone Pro may drop the Action button
item.description:
Apple is rumored to merge the iPhone's Action button into Camera Control starting with next year's models, according to leaker Instant Digital on Weibo. A single press of the combined button would open the camera, while a long press would trigger whatever function was assigned to the Action button — and the dedicated Action button itself would disappear.

The Action button replaced the mute switch on the iPhone 15 Pro in 2023, but the iPhone Duo already skipped it, and the rumor suggests the phase-out will extend across the iPhone 20 range in the second half of next year. The arrangement is plausible given how the two buttons already work, though don't expect the old mute switch to return — the combined button takes over both roles.

Sources

item.title: Apple faces congressional scrutiny over ICE-tracking apps and Trump donations
item.description:
Apple is among the tech giants facing congressional investigations as Democrats prepare to take control of both chambers in January, according to Reuters and The Washington Post. The scrutiny spans the company's handling of ICE-tracking apps on the App Store and donations to President Trump's planned White House ballroom — Apple reportedly gave $25 million.

Senator Richard Blumenthal, the incoming leader of the Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations, has ordered Amazon, Apple, Google, Meta, Microsoft, Nvidia, and others to turn over documentation about the ballroom donations, with subpoenas threatened if they don't comply. The inquiries are still in the early stages, but they signal a much more confrontational relationship between Apple and Congress.

Sources

  • 9to5Mac: Report: Apple faces congressional scrutiny over ICE tracking apps and Trump donations
  • AppleInsider: Democrat orders Apple to disclose details of Trump ballroom donation

item.title: Apple confirms a $7.5 billion bond sale after strong investor demand
item.description:
Apple has confirmed a $7.5 billion bond sale, slightly larger than the roughly $7 billion expected when the offering was first reported. The final pricing term sheet filed with the SEC shows the company issuing bonds in seven series maturing between 2028 and 2036.

The deal comes after a strong quarter and robust investor demand, and it's a routine move for Apple, which regularly taps the debt markets to fund dividends and share buybacks rather than repatriating overseas cash. The size and the seven-tranche structure suggest the company found eager buyers even in a crowded corporate bond market.

Sources

The headline deals: the 13-inch M5 MacBook Air with 16GB of RAM and 1TB of storage is down to $1,349, a $250 discount, while the Apple Watch Ultra 4 is $99 off at $699.99 and the previous-gen Ultra 3 with a Milanese Loop has fallen to $649 — $250 off and the lowest price on record.

AirPods Max 2 is $100 off, AirPods Pro 3 is $50 off, and B&H is throwing in a free $150 gift card with the brand-new PROLED MacBook Pro. Best Buy's early sale runs through November with new doorbusters each week, so the deepest discounts are still ahead — but several of this week's prices are already at or near all-time lows.

item.title: Touchscreen MacBook Pro reviews: the screen steals the show, touch is a bonus
item.description:
The first reviews of Apple's touchscreen MacBook Pro with its tandem-OLED PROLED XDR display are out ahead of Friday's launch, and the verdict is near-unanimous: the screen is the real star, while touch is a pleasant extra rather than a game-changer. The Verge's David Pierce said touch hasn't “meaningfully changed the laptop experience” in his testing, though he still recommends the machine for the display and other upgrades, and reviewers across the board praised the panel while wincing at the price.

The new 14- and 16-inch models also bring a slimmer design, M5 Pro and M5 Max chips, and the return of the glowing Apple logo — which Apple now explains how to switch off. Preordered machines are already arriving in Australia and New Zealand, and Apple showed off the touchscreen in a nearly four-hour livestream with musician Labrinth building a song in Logic Pro by tapping the display.

item.title: iOS 27.3 public beta arrives with a redesigned Health app and bigger Siri AI
item.description:
Apple seeded the first public betas of iOS 27.3, iPadOS 27.3, macOS 27.3, tvOS 27.3, and watchOS 27.3, two days after the developer builds. It's a major update: Safari gets vertical tabs and Adaptive Dark Mode, Siri AI gains more abilities across Apple's apps (and developers can now build actions for it), and the redesigned Health app — briefly seen during iOS 27.2 testing — returns with custom Insights and Longevity information. The iPhone Duo gets Reachability and a reworked keyboard.

Separately, Apple quietly dropped the Siri AI waitlist for most users: an updated support document says the assistant now downloads automatically after opting in, with the waitlist reserved only for times of high demand. The change follows two months of server-load testing since Siri AI launched in beta in September. Apple warns the betas still have bugs, so anyone relying on a mission-critical device may want to wait.

item.title: iPhone Duo: Apple surveys buyers on the crease, and the fold test passes 260,000 folds
item.description:
Apple is emailing surveys to iPhone Duo buyers asking why they bought Apple's first foldable, how visible they find the display crease, whether the under-display camera is distracting, and how the camera performs — an early signal the company is gathering feedback to shape the next generation. Meanwhile, CNET's livestreamed durability test has folded and unfolded a Duo more than 260,000 times over the past week, with the device still going.

Launch-day buyers face a decision now: the standard 14-day return window for October 23 purchases expires Friday, November 6. And reviews note the Duo's multitasking, while a first for iPhone, is limited — two apps side by side, but no iPad-style windowing, so it stops short of turning the foldable into a true multitasking machine.

item.title: Apple's quarter in numbers: record Mac sales, half of all smartphone revenue, iPad slump
item.description:
On this week's earnings call, Apple CEO John Ternus said the company sold more Macs in fiscal 2026 than in any previous fiscal year, a record set despite supply constraints on several models, with the MacBook Neo and MacBook Pro driving sales. Supply-chain reports suggest Apple wants suppliers to build 16 million MacBook Neos in 2027, double this year's expected volume.

The iPhone picture was just as strong: Counterpoint Research reports Apple captured half of all global smartphone revenue in the third calendar quarter, its highest-ever Q3 revenue. The weak spot was iPad, where shipments fell 27.5% year over year as the whole tablet market plunged — though Apple still held its lead in the category.

item.title: Apple files for a $7 billion bond sale — and investors want four times that
item.description:
Apple filed a preliminary prospectus with the SEC for a new bond offering of about $7 billion across seven series, its first bond sale since May 2025, when it raised $4.5 billion. The filing doesn't specify final interest rates, but the proceeds would typically fund stock buybacks, dividends, and other corporate expenses.

Demand was overwhelming: reports say investors placed orders worth roughly four times the planned offering. That appetite underscores how cheaply Apple can still borrow despite the size of the deal — and how eager the bond market remains for Apple paper even as the company sits on enormous cash reserves.

item.title: Creator Studio updates roll out, but Logic Pro's new AI assistant is subscription-only
item.description:
Apple began rolling out the Creator Studio app updates it announced last month, starting with Logic Pro for Mac. The update brings a Liquid Glass redesign, an AI-powered Intelligent Assistant that builds beats from natural-language prompts using a mix of Apple Intelligence and OpenAI models, and a redesigned browser that centralizes project assets. The remaining app updates arrive later in November.

There's a catch that has Logic Pro owners talking: the Intelligent Assistant requires a $12.99/month (or $129/year) Apple Creator Studio subscription, and is not available to buyers of the $199.99 one-time-purchase version of Logic Pro — a notable line between Apple's perpetual license and its subscription tier.

item.title: HomeView hub has 8GB of RAM — and code hints it may get third-party chatbots
item.description:
MacRumors confirmed that the A18 chip in Apple's new HomeView smart home hub is paired with 8GB of RAM — the same pairing as in iPhone 16 models and the MacBook Neo, though Apple doesn't list it in the specs.

More interesting is what code in the iOS 27.3 beta suggests is coming: the software HomeView uses to display apps from a connected iPhone or iPad has gained a “Conversational Apps” category, pointing to future support for third-party AI chatbots like ChatGPT and Claude, plus preparations for two-way audio routing, session management, and interruptions. The feature isn't fully wired up yet, and Apple hasn't announced anything — but it's a sign HomeView may be more open to outside AI than expected.

item.title: Apple TV and Arcade: Bad Monkey returns in December, Crossy Road Rush and NBA 2K27 arrive

Apple TV set a December 2 premiere for season 2 of Bad Monkey, the Vince Vaughn comedy from the creator of Ted Lasso and Shrinking, with John Malkovich and Yvonne Strahovski joining the cast and a new trailer out now. Apple also announced Lenni, a new comedy-drama starring Toni Collette as a divorced social worker, now in production in Sydney. On the gaming side, Apple Arcade added four games, headlined by Crossy Road Rush — a new entry in the series with 50 hand-curated levels and four-player co-op — and NBA 2K27 Arcade Edition, which brings the WNBA to the service for the first time, with all 15 teams and 180 players in Quick Match and Blacktop modes.

item.title: Siri AI expands fast in the iOS 27.3 betas — and drops its waitlist
item.description:
The first iOS 27.3 developer betas, released this week, bring a substantial expansion of Siri AI — and reviewers say the pace is the story. Federico Viticci, writing at MacStories, found the new Siri AI Developer Preview shows Apple executing fast on its AI plan, with an orchestration layer flexible enough to make the assistant more useful simply by adding tools. The betas extend Siri AI to Safari and add new developer support, and Xcode 27.3 lets developers test Siri AI integration in their own apps.

Not everything landed well: hands-on testing of the new Audio Intelligence features — Siri Recaps, which summarize meetings and conversations, and Live Rewind — found them more like checked boxes than fully realized tools, raising privacy and usefulness questions even with Apple's on-device boundaries. Meanwhile, Apple quietly dropped the Siri AI waitlist, keeping it only as a fallback during periods of high demand.

item.title: Apple will scan publicly shared iCloud links for harmful content starting in iOS 27.3
item.description:
Apple will begin checking publicly shared iCloud content for harmful material with the 27.3 updates across iOS, iPadOS, macOS, and visionOS. Photos in iCloud Photos and files in iCloud Drive shared via the "Anyone with the link" option will be "made accessible to Apple" for a content check, with violations risking removal of the content, account bans, or referral to law enforcement.

Apple hasn't precisely defined "harmful content," but the likely targets are malware, malicious files, and child sexual abuse material. The trade-off is explicit: sharing via a public link already strips end-to-end encryption, even for users who have it enabled. Private, end-to-end-encrypted iCloud sharing is unaffected — the checks apply only to content opened up to anyone with a link.

item.title: Apple is putting its own employees on an AI budget
item.description:
Apple is curtailing how much its own staff can spend on third-party AI tools, according to Bloomberg. In October, some engineers saw their daily AI allowance cut from $300 to $200, and further reductions are reportedly coming, with some engineers dropping to $100 a day. Many teams outside engineering already sit at a $100 daily cap, and some could be limited to as little as $25.

The cuts come as Apple pushes teams toward cheaper models or on-device AI, and employees who need more can ask executives for an increase. Engineers keep the largest budgets, since AI coding assistance and bug hunting are core to their work — but the message is clear: even Apple, now racing to build out Siri AI, thinks its AI tooling bill has gotten too big.

item.title: AAPL closes at another record high after the election and Q4 results
item.description:
Apple shares closed Wednesday at a record $349.51, up 5.31% on the day, after touching an intraday high of $354.50. The stock rebounded sharply from its post-earnings dip following Monday's record fiscal fourth quarter, riding a broader market rally after the election. The previous record close was $332.93.

Six Colors' annual chart breakdown of Apple's fiscal 2026 shows why investors are enthusiastic: the year closed with an all-time quarterly revenue record and a record fiscal year overall. The rally caps a strong run for Apple stock into the holiday quarter, with the new MacBook Pro and iPhone lineup now in full swing.

item.title: macOS 27.3 brings Live Activities to every Mac — and kills off compromised certificates
item.description:
The first macOS 27.3 developer beta brings Live Activities — previously an iPhone and iPad feature — to all supported Macs, not just the new PROLED MacBook Pro with its Dynamic Island. On other Macs, Live Activities from apps like Music, Clock, and Voice Memos appear in the menu bar, showing timers, playback, and screen recording at a glance. Third-party apps can adopt it too.

The same beta also delivers an important security fix: it fully blocks the shockingly weak eMudhra certificates discovered in October, removing them from the system's certificate store so command-line tools can no longer accept them. A macOS 27.2.1 update is expected sooner with the same fix. Smaller touches include native Markdown rendering in Quick Look, so pressing Space on a .md file shows styled headings, lists, and links.

item.title: PROLED MacBook Pro launches November 6 — and the non-touch Pro may be on borrowed time
item.description:
Apple's new MacBook Pro with its Tandem OLED PROLED display arrives November 6, and Apple is marking the launch with an all-night livestream in which musician Labrinth will produce a full song from scratch at the Tower Theatre store in downtown Los Angeles, putting the machine through its paces live.

Meanwhile, Bloomberg's Mark Gurman reports Apple will likely consolidate its high-end MacBook Pro lineup around touchscreen models. The company is still selling mini-LED M5 Pro and M5 Max models alongside the touchscreen versions, which cost $400 more — but Gurman argues the cost of supporting parallel lines across development, production, and promotion makes convergence likely. The touchscreen Pro may soon be the only high-end Pro.

item.title: Developers can now try to talk you out of canceling a subscription
item.description:
Apple has added a subscription retention feature for developers: when a subscriber goes to cancel an auto-renewable subscription, the app can now show a retention message in the cancellation flow, including text, images, or a special offer such as a discount. Developers configure the messages in App Store Connect, with options for subscriber eligibility and how long to wait before showing another one.

A separate Retention Messaging API, available by request, lets developers choose which message to show based on a subscriber's details. For users, expect the familiar "are you sure?" moment to get more persuasive — a last-minute discount may now appear right when you're about to cancel.

item.title: A new persistent iPhone jailbreak thwarts Lockdown Mode
item.description:
A hacker group called Calif has demonstrated a new iPhone jailbreak that persists even with Lockdown Mode enabled — and survives an update to iOS 27.2. In a video posted to X, the group shows an iPhone 18 Pro with Lockdown Mode on running the jailbreak, a direct challenge to Apple's hardest security setting, designed to protect high-profile targets from sophisticated attacks.

Apple claimed in March 2026 that Lockdown Mode had achieved a 100% protection rate since 2022, so the demonstration is a notable dent in that record. Details of the exploit are still thin, and there's no indication it affects ordinary users — Lockdown Mode is aimed at people facing grave, targeted threats — but Apple will almost certainly be working on a patch.

Sources

item.title: iOS 27.3 beta 1 arrives with a bigger Siri AI, Safari overhaul, and a redesigned Health app
item.description:
Apple seeded the first developer betas of iOS 27.3, iPadOS 27.3, macOS Golden Gate 27.3, watchOS 27.3, tvOS 27.3, and visionOS 27.3, and it's shaping up to be the biggest update to iOS 27 since launch. Siri AI gains a long list of new in-app and cross-app actions, Safari gets a vertical tabs layout and an adaptive dark mode for sites without one, and StandBy comes to iPhone 11 and newer with the iPhone Duo's revamped design.

The beta also reintroduces the redesigned Health app — pulled from the 27.2 release — with new Insights and Longevity tabs and AI-powered Personal Guidance, brings Apple Intelligence features to China for the first time, and adds Live Rewind and Siri Recap to Apple Watch. A public release is likely months away, but developers can test now.

item.title: Apple opens Siri AI to all developers with new 'app skills'
item.description:
For the first time, any developer can integrate their app with Siri AI. A new Developer Preview in the 27.3 betas lets apps define 'app skills' that teach Siri how to carry out complex, multi-step actions — a big step beyond the small set of supported schemas the first Siri AI versions offered.

The preview is a sneak peek ahead of a customer launch in a few months, and it signals Apple's plan to make Siri a genuine platform for third-party services rather than a first-party-only assistant. Developers can start building and submitting integrations now, with the features shipping as part of iOS 27.3 and its companion releases.

item.title: iPad mini (A20 Pro) reviews: a great little tablet, still stuck at 60Hz
item.description:
Reviews of the new iPad mini landed ahead of its Friday launch, and the verdict is broadly warm with one recurring complaint. Reviewers praise the OLED display, the new design, and the acoustic display that fires sound from the front panel — though some note you can feel the whole tablet vibrate at high volume, and the two color options are, in MKBHD's words, 'annoyingly, slightly not black and slightly not white.'

The sticking point is the screen's 60Hz refresh rate: no ProMotion, despite the OLED upgrade, which several reviewers call frustrating and hard to justify. Battery life, meanwhile, appears better than Apple claims. Overall, it's a modern multitasker that broadens the mini's appeal — just don't expect a buttery display.

item.title: Apple posts record $114.5 billion quarter as iPhone sales climb
item.description:
Apple reported fourth-quarter 2026 revenue of $114.5 billion, a quarterly record that narrowly beat Wall Street's $113.4 billion consensus. iPhone revenue rose year over year to $57.58 billion — notably without the non-Pro iPhone, which has been a driver in China — and CEO John Ternus fronted the earnings call for the first time.

Analysts were broadly positive on the results, though commentary also noted that Apple's analyst calls have been scripted for decades, a point raised after criticism of Ternus reading from a script. The record quarter caps a year in which Apple's staggered iPhone release schedule appears to be paying off.

item.title: Apple explicitly bans employees from trading on insider info in prediction markets
item.description:
Apple has updated its insider trading policy to explicitly prohibit employees and contractors from using confidential company information to bet on prediction markets. The markets, which skirt the legal definition of gambling, let users bet on everything from product colors to launch timing — exactly the kind of nonpublic detail Apple staff might know.

The move closes a gray area as prediction markets have gone mainstream in the US, and it puts Apple employees on notice that insider-trading rules apply to these platforms just as they do to the stock market.

item.title: Fitness+ goes to the gym with personalized Gym Strength plans
item.description:
Apple Fitness+ is expanding beyond home workouts with Gym Strength, a new feature in the iOS 27.3 beta that builds a four-week strength plan around your goals, experience, schedule, and available equipment. You pick workout days, body areas, and session length, and get exercise, rep, set, and load recommendations plus short trainer video demos.

Plans adapt week to week based on your progress, and Apple Watch wearers can log sessions from the wrist. It's Apple's most direct play yet for gym-goers, turning Fitness+ from a living-room service into a full training companion.

item.title: Apple Music adds Selfie Sing karaoke videos
item.description:
iOS 27.3 adds Selfie Sing to Apple Music: a karaoke mode that records you singing along while lyrics scroll on screen, with a dedicated Selfie Sing playlist to get started. It builds on Apple Music Sing, which already let you lower vocals and follow highlighted lyrics — now the performance itself is the point.

It's a small, fun feature rather than a platform shift, but it fits Apple's pattern of turning Music into a more social, participatory app, and it's the kind of thing likely to show up in a lot of group chats this holiday season.

item.title: Apple posts a record $114.5 billion quarter in John Ternus's first earnings report as CEO
item.description:
Apple closed fiscal 2026 with a record fourth quarter: $114.5 billion in revenue, up 12% year over year, and $30.7 billion in profit. iPhone revenue jumped 17.5% to $57.6 billion — a record for the quarter even without a new standard iPhone model — while Mac revenue rose 23.7% and Services grew 9.8% to $31.6 billion. iPad fell 10.4% and Wearables dropped 7.9%.

It was the first earnings report under new CEO John Ternus, who took over from Tim Cook on September 1, and the first call to feature COO Sabih Khan alongside CFO Kevan Parekh. The results beat Wall Street expectations, though the stock still dipped in after-hours trading once the call ended — a familiar pattern for Apple, whose quarter was strong enough to top even the COVID-fueled 2020 holiday quarter.

item.title: The memory crisis dominates the call: costs still climbing, iPhone Duo shortages with no end in sight
item.description:
If one theme defined the earnings call, it was memory. Ternus called current memory pricing 'unprecedented,' warning costs rose in the September quarter and will be worse in December and beyond, squeezing margins alongside Siri AI spending. Apple dodged questions about further price hikes, and its inventory ballooned to $14.54 billion as it stockpiled components.

The iPhone Duo, Apple's first foldable, remains badly supply-constrained: Ternus told Reuters Apple 'isn't able to predict' when supply and demand will balance, and UBS data puts average buyer wait times at 89 days. Mac and iPad supplies will also stay tight through the holidays, so anyone eyeing a new iPad mini or MacBook Pro may face delays.

item.title: Apple forecasts its biggest quarter ever, spends a record $45.77 billion on R&D, and passes 2.5 billion active devices
item.description:
Despite the supply constraints, Apple told investors the December quarter should be the best revenue quarter in company history, with CFO Kevan Parekh pointing to as much as 10% year-over-year growth. The company also disclosed a record $45.77 billion in fiscal 2026 R&D spending, up 32%, and confirmed it has received most of its reciprocal-tariff refunds from the U.S. government.

Two scale milestones framed the call: Apple's installed base has passed 2.5 billion active devices, and Siri now handles more than 2.5 billion requests a day — the audience Ternus is betting on as the rebuilt Siri rolls out. The board kept the quarterly dividend unchanged at $0.27 per share.

item.title: Supreme Court won't hear Apple v. Epic until January 2027
item.description:
The U.S. Supreme Court has scheduled oral arguments in Apple's appeal in its long-running Epic Games case for January 2027, pushing the timeline back further even as battles in the lower courts continue. The appeal concerns the lower court's authority in the case, and the delay raises the possibility that Epic's remaining claims could be rendered moot before the justices ever weigh in. For now, the App Store status quo — and the litigation over it — grinds on into another year.

item.title: App Store to require 18+ ratings for dating apps and AI romantic companions
item.description:
Apple announced new App Store age-rating rules: starting November 16, developers must disclose whether their apps include real-world location sharing or dating and relationship features, including virtual companions that engage in romantic or sexual content. Apps with those features will require an 18+ age rating, with full disclosure required by January 2027.

The move extends Apple's self-reported age-rating system, introduced in 2025 to get ahead of tightening global age-gating regulations, and lands as regulators worldwide scrutinize both location sharing and AI companions aimed at younger users.

item.title: Hundreds of AI apps with hidden deepfake tools slipped past App Store review
item.description:
An investigation published November 2 uncovered a network of more than 400 connected apps and web domains that presented themselves as harmless AI services — pet portraits, language lessons, fitness coaching — but could load tools for generating sexually explicit and violent deepfakes from uploaded photos. The apps, apparently created by a single Chinese organization, passed App Store and Google Play review by hiding the abusive features behind ordinary ones.

Apple has removed 19 of the apps so far. The episode is an embarrassing miss for App Store review and a reminder of how easily deepfake abuse tools can be disguised as mainstream AI apps.

item.title: Apple warned users in 99 countries of possible mercenary spyware attacks
item.description:
Apple recently sent threat notifications to users in 99 countries warning they may have been targeted by mercenary spyware, according to reports. German authorities are investigating claims that lawmakers and government officials were among those targeted. The notifications are Apple's standard warning for the kind of sophisticated, state-linked attacks that go far beyond ordinary malware — and the sheer breadth, 99 countries at once, underscores how widespread commercial spyware targeting has become.

item.title: HomeView Ultra details leak: a bigger, swiveling smart-home hub for 2027 — and the current HomeView may double as a security camera
item.description:
The Information reports Apple is developing a larger, robotic HomeView — dubbed 'HomeView Ultra' or 'HomeView Max' in rumors — with a 9-inch display on a swiveling arm, a design said to resemble the old iMac G4 or Pixar's lamp mascot. It's expected in 2027 or 2028, after the standard HomeView reaches homes next week.

Separately, code sleuths found strings in HomeView Software 27.2 suggesting the hub itself could serve as a HomeKit Secure Video camera, with modes for Off, Detect Activity, Stream, and Stream & Allow Recording, plus scheduling based on whether residents are home, away, or asleep — with privacy protections for household members.

item.title: Also from Apple: Affinity lands on iPad, tvOS 27.2 build drops ahead of the new Apple TV 4K, and iOS 27.2.1 is on the way
item.description:
Canva released Affinity for iPad, bringing its free all-in-one design app — vector, photo, and layout tools unified on desktop last year — to Apple's tablet with a new touch-first Sketch Studio for Apple Pencil. The desktop app has drawn more than seven million users since the relaunch.

Meanwhile, Apple shipped a new tvOS 27.2 build for the fourth-generation Apple TV 4K ahead of the new model's November 13 launch, and iOS 27.2.1 is showing up in logs as a minor bug-fix update, with the first iOS 27.3 beta expected as soon as tomorrow.
